Ch. 1 // A Portrait of Charles T. Munger
By Michael Broggie

A Portrait of Charles T. Munger查理·芒格传略

Behind the extraordinary story of Berkshire Hathaway2Berkshire Hathaway伯克希尔·哈撒韦 are two financial geniuses: the widely acclaimed Warren Buffett25Warren Buffett沃伦·巴菲特 and his “silent partner,”3Buffett’s silent partner巴菲特的沉默伙伴 Charlie Munger, who relishes his obscurity.

伯克希尔·哈撒韦2Berkshire Hathaway伯克希尔·哈撒韦（Berkshire Hathaway）非凡成就的背后，是两位金融天才：广受赞誉的沃伦·巴菲特25Warren Buffett沃伦·巴菲特（Warren Buffett），以及他那以低调为乐的“沉默伙伴”——查理·芒格1Charles T. Munger查尔斯·T·芒格（Charlie Munger）。

Charlie is Warren’s friend, lawyer, adviser, devil’s advocate (Warren once called him the “abominable no-man”), and one of the largest stockholders in one of the most successful publicly traded companies in American business history. Since 1964, when Warren—and, some years later, Charlie—assumed management of Berkshire, its market value has increased an astonishing 13,500 times, from $10 million to roughly $135 billion, without much of an increase in outstanding shares. Such phenomenal growth is the singular achievement of these two unassuming Midwesterners, who combine their synergistic abilities to recognize and seize opportunities other businessmen consistently overlook.

查理是沃伦的朋友、律师、顾问、唱反调者（沃伦曾称他为“可恶的‘说不先生’”），也是美国商业史上最成功的上市公司之一的头号大股东之一。自1964年沃伦接管伯克希尔——数年后查理也加入管理层——以来，其市值令人惊叹地增长了13500倍，从1000万美元增至约1350亿美元，而流通股数几乎没有增加。如此惊人的增长，是这两位谦逊的中西部人独一无二的成就；他们合力发挥协同的才能，识别并抓住了其他商界人士屡屡错过的机会。

While Warren is one of the most admired and publicized business leaders in the country, Charlie has purposefully sidestepped the limelight, choosing relative anonymity instead. To better understand this complex and highly private businessman, we must start at the beginning. Charles Thomas Munger was born on January 1, 1924, in America’s heartland, Omaha, Nebraska. Many notables share his Midwestern roots: Will Rogers, Henry Fonda, John Pershing,4John Pershing约翰·潘兴 Harry Truman, Walt Disney,5Walt Disney华特·迪士尼 Ann Landers, Gerald Ford6Gerald Ford杰拉尔德·福特—and, of course, Warren Buffett.

尽管沃伦是美国最受敬仰、曝光度最高的商界领袖之一，查理却刻意避开聚光灯，宁可相对默默无闻。为了更好地理解这位复杂而极度注重隐私的商人，我们必须从头说起。查尔斯·托马斯·芒格1Charles T. Munger查尔斯·T·芒格于1924年1月1日出生在美国腹地——内布拉斯加州（Nebraska）的奥马哈（Omaha）。许多知名人士与他有着相同的中西部渊源：威尔·罗杰斯（Will Rogers）、亨利·方达（Henry Fonda）、约翰·潘兴4John Pershing约翰·潘兴（John Pershing）、哈里·杜鲁门（Harry Truman）、华特·迪士尼5Walt Disney华特·迪士尼（Walt Disney）、安·兰德斯（Ann Landers）、杰拉尔德·福特6Gerald Ford杰拉尔德·福特（Gerald Ford）——当然，还有沃伦·巴菲特。

“Charlie has purposefully sidestepped the limelight, choosing relative anonymity instead.”查理刻意避开了聚光灯，宁可选择相对的默默无闻。

Charlie initially crossed paths with the Buffett family during the formative years of his life when he worked at, Buffett & Son, an upscale grocery store in Omaha, about six blocks from the Munger household. The boss and part owner was Warren’s grandfather, Ernest. A strict disciplinarian, he scheduled his young workers for 12-hour shifts with no meals or breaks. According to Charlie, his boss’s staunch anti-socialist attitude was manifested in his rule requiring the boys to present two pennies at the end of their shifts to cover their share of the cost of the new Social Security Act. In return, they received a $2 daily wage—along with a considerable lecture about the evils of socialism.

查理早年初次与巴菲特家族产生交集，是在他于巴菲特父子店（Buffett and Son）打工的时候。那是奥马哈一家高档食品杂货店，距芒格1Charles T. Munger查尔斯·T·芒格家约六个街区。老板兼部分店主是沃伦的祖父欧内斯特（Ernest）。他是个严厉的纪律执行者，安排年轻店员每天上12小时班，其间不准吃饭，也不准休息。据查理说，老板坚定的反社会主义态度体现在一条规矩上：下班时，男孩们必须交上两美分，以支付新《社会安全法》（Social Security Act）摊到他们头上的那部分费用。作为回报，他们拿到2美元的日薪——外加一大通关于社会主义罪恶的说教。

The arduous working conditions in the Buffett grocery store had a lasting influence on both Charlie and Warren. Warren, six years younger, served his hard times under Grandpa Ernest several years after his future business partner had moved on.

巴菲特杂货店的艰苦劳动条件对查理和沃伦都产生了持久的影响。小查理六岁的沃伦，在他未来的生意伙伴离开数年之后，也在欧内斯特爷爷手下吃了同样的苦。

Notables with Midwestern roots来自中西部的名人

Charlie’s formal education began at Dundee Elementary School, where he and his younger sisters, Mary and Carol, were indoctrinated with ethical homilies. Charlie’s teachers remember a smart kid who was also inclined to be a bit of a wiseacre. He enjoyed challenging the conventional wisdom of teachers and fellow students with his ever-increasing knowledge gained through voracious reading,9Voracious reading如饥似渴的阅读 particularly biographies. Today, he can’t remember the first time he was exposed to the aphorisms of Ben Franklin,10Ben Franklin本·富兰克林 but they fueled an ineffaceable admiration for the eclectic and eccentric statesman and inventor. Charlie’s parents, Al and Florence Munger, encouraged reading and gave each of their children several books at Christmas, usually devoured by that night.

查理的正式教育始于邓迪小学（Dundee Elementary School），他和妹妹玛丽（Mary）、卡萝尔（Carol）在那里接受了道德箴言的熏陶。查理的老师记得，这是个聪明、又有点爱耍小聪明的孩子。他喜欢用如饥似渴的阅读9Voracious reading如饥似渴的阅读——尤其是传记——所积累起来的日益增长的知识，去挑战老师和同学们的成见。如今，他已记不清第一次接触本杰明·富兰克林10Ben Franklin本·富兰克林（Ben Franklin）格言警句是在何时，但这些格言点燃了他对这位博采众长而又特立独行的政治家兼发明家难以磨灭的景仰。查理的父母阿尔（Al）和弗洛伦斯·芒格（Florence Munger）鼓励阅读，每年圣诞节都给每个孩子几本书，而那些书通常当晚就被啃光了。

At the nearby home of the Mungers’ close friends, the Davises, Charlie often read the medical journals belonging to Dr. Ed Davis, who was both his father’s best friend and a family physician. Charlie’s early exposure to Dr. Davis’s medical library spawned a lifelong interest in science. By the time he was 14, the precocious learner had also become one of the doctor’s best friends. Charlie became so interested in medicine that he watched motion pictures of Dr. Davis, a urologist, performing surgery and became fascinated with the statistical outcomes of similar procedures in the field.

在芒格家的世交戴维斯（Davis）家附近，查理常常翻阅埃德·戴维斯医生（Dr. Ed Davis）的医学期刊；戴维斯既是他父亲最好的朋友，也是家里的家庭医生。查理早年接触戴维斯医生的医学藏书，萌生了对科学终生的兴趣。到14岁时，这个早慧的少年也成了医生最好的朋友之一。查理对医学的兴趣如此之浓，以至于他观看泌尿科医生戴维斯实施手术的影片，并迷上了该领域类似手术的统计结果。

“Charlie’s teachers remember a smart kid who was also inclined to be a bit of a wiseacre.”查理的老师记得，这是个聪明孩子，也多少有点贫嘴。

At home, Charlie developed a fondness for raising hamsters11Raising hamsters养仓鼠 and periodically traded them with other children. Even at an early age, Charlie showed a sagacious negotiating ability and usually gained a bigger specimen or one with unusual coloring. When his brood grew to 35 animals,12When his brood grew to 35 animals他的宠物增长到35只 his mother ordered an end to his hobby because of the pungent odor from his basement hamster farm. One of his sisters remembered years later that the family had to endure the incessant squeaking of hungry hamsters until Charlie arrived home from school to feed them.

在家里，查理喜欢养仓鼠11Raising hamsters养仓鼠，并时常拿它们和其他孩子交换。查理很小就显露出精明的谈判能力，往往能换到一只更大的，或是毛色罕见的个体。当他的“族群”繁殖到35只时，母亲因为地下室仓鼠养殖场散发的刺鼻气味，勒令他停止这项爱好。多年后，他的一位妹妹还记得，在查理放学回家喂食之前，全家人不得不忍受饥饿仓鼠无休止的吱吱尖叫。

Charlie attended Central High School,13Charlie Munger c. 1940s查理·芒格（约1940年代） a very large public school that was recognized as a good college preparatory school. The teachers, mostly women, were dedicated to their work and to their students. The Central High curriculum provided a conventional classic education, in which Charlie naturally excelled because of his logically driven, inquiring mind.

查理就读于中央高中（Central High School），这是一所规模很大的公立学校，被认为是一所优质的大学预备学校。老师们多为女性，对工作和对学生都尽职尽责。中央高中的课程提供传统的经典教育，查理凭借其逻辑驱动、求知若渴的头脑，自然出类拔萃。

Throughout elementary and secondary school, Charlie was younger and smaller than his classmates, having been moved ahead in elementary school after his mother taught him to read phonically. Too small to compete in regular high school sports, he joined the rifle team, earned a varsity letter, and eventually became team captain. His letterman’s sweater14Letterman’s sweater莱特曼的毛衣 (“a large letter on a very small chest” is Charlie’s memory) attracted attention from coeds who wondered how such a scrawny kid could earn a varsity letter. Fortunately for Charlie, his father was an avid outdoorsman and duck hunter and took joy in his son’s marksmanship.

从小学到中学，查理都比同学年纪小、个子矮——这是因为母亲教他用拼读法识字后，他在小学被跳级了。身材太小，无法参加常规的高中体育运动，他便加入了步枪队，赢得校队荣誉，并最终成为队长。他那件校队毛衣（查理的记忆是“很小的胸口上绣着大大的字母”）引得女生们侧目，她们纳闷这个瘦巴巴的小孩怎么也能拿到校队荣誉。对查理而言幸运的是，父亲是个狂热的户外爱好者和猎鸭人，对儿子的枪法颇为得意。

Omaha in the 1920s was the proverbial melting pot; different races and religions mixed socially and commercially, and crime was practically unknown. Doors and vehicles were left unlocked, and a person’s word was trusted implicitly. Kids played kick the can on warm summer evenings and went to Saturday matinees to see the latest talkies, such as King Kong,16King Kong金刚 a favorite of 8-year-old Charlie.

20世纪20年代的奥马哈是名副其实的大熔炉；不同种族和宗教的人在社会上和生意场中交融共处，犯罪几乎闻所未闻。门户和车辆都不上锁，一个人的承诺会被无条件信任。孩子们在温暖的夏夜玩“踢罐头”游戏，周六下午去看最新上映的有声电影，比如《金刚16King Kong金刚》（King Kong），那是八岁查理的最爱。

The 1930s brought hard times, and Omaha experienced the severity of the Great Depression. Charlie’s observations of the plight of those less fortunate made a lasting impression. He saw hobos roaming the streets looking for handouts and others who were willing to sweep a driveway or porch in exchange for a sandwich. Thanks to family connections, Charlie landed a boring job counting passersby; it paid 40xa2 an hour. Charlie preferred this work to carrying heavy boxes of groceries.

30年代带来了艰难时世，奥马哈也深切体会到了大萧条17The Great Depression大萧条（Great Depression）的严酷。查理对不幸者窘境的观察留下了持久的印象。他看见流浪汉在街头游荡乞讨，也看见有人愿意清扫车道或门廊，以换取一个三明治。凭借家庭关系，查理得到了一份数来往行人的无聊差事，时薪40美分。比起搬运沉重的食品箱，查理更喜欢这份工作。

“Charlie’s observations of the plight of those less fortunate made a lasting impression.”查理对不幸者处境的观察，留下了持久的印记。

Charlie’s grandfather was a respected federal judge, and his father followed in his footsteps to become a prosperous lawyer. Charlie’s immediate family was not dramatically affected by the Depression, but some members of Charlie’s extended family were. This era provided real learning experiences for young Charlie. He witnessed the generosity and business acumen of his grandfather as he helped rescue a small bank in Stromsburg, Nebraska, that was owned by Charlie’s uncle Tom. Because of the miserable economy and drought-damaged crops, the bank’s farm-based clients were defaulting on loans. Tom had rolled up $35,000 in uncollectible notes when he called upon Grandpa Munger for support. The judge risked nearly half of his assets by exchanging $35,000 in sound first mortgages for the bank’s weak loans, thus enabling Tom to open his doors after Roosevelt’s bank holiday. The judge eventually recovered most of his investment, but not until a great many years later.

查理的祖父是一位受人尊敬的联邦法官，父亲则追随其脚步，成为一名成功的律师。查理的直系家庭并未受到大萧条17The Great Depression大萧条的剧烈冲击，但一些旁系亲属却深受其害。这个时代为年轻的查理提供了真切的学习体验。他亲眼目睹了祖父的慷慨与商业头脑——祖父出手救助了内布拉斯加州斯特龙斯堡（Stromsburg）一家由查理的叔叔汤姆（Tom）拥有的小银行。由于经济凋敝、旱灾毁了庄稼，该银行的农场客户纷纷违约欠贷。汤姆累积了3.5万美元无法收回的票据，才向芒格爷爷求援。这位法官冒着近半身家的风险，用3.5万美元稳健的第一抵押权，换下银行那些不良贷款，从而使汤姆得以在罗斯福（Roosevelt）的银行休假令之后重新开张。法官最终收回了大部分投资，但那是许多年以后的事了。

Judge Munger also sent his daughter’s husband, a musician, to pharmacy school and helped him buy a well-located pharmacy that had closed because of the Depression. The business prospered and secured the future for Charlie’s aunt. Charlie learned that by supporting each other, the Mungers weathered the worst economic collapse in the nation’s history.

芒格法官还把女婿——一位音乐家——送去药剂学校，并帮他买下一家因大萧条17The Great Depression大萧条而倒闭、地段极佳的药房。生意兴旺，为查理的姑姑保住了未来。查理由此懂得，芒格一家人互相扶持，扛过了美国历史上最严重的经济崩溃。

“By supporting each other, the Mungers weathered the worst economic collapse in the nation’s history.”靠着彼此扶持，芒格一家挺过了美国历史上最严重的经济崩溃。

Fortunately, Al Munger’s law practice prospered during the Depression and was given a boost when the United States Supreme Court agreed to review a tax case involving a small soap-making company he represented. Coincidently, the huge Colgate-Palmolive Company17Colgate-Palmolive Company高露洁-棕榄公司 was also affected by the court’s decision. Concerned that the Midwestern attorney didn’t have the requisite experience to argue successfully before the highest court, Colgate offered to pay Al liberally to step aside and allow a famous New York attorney to take his place. The big-city lawyer lost the case while Al pocketed a substantial fee. Later, Al joked that he could have lost the case just as well for a much smaller fee. The amount of the fee has never been revealed, but it was enough, when combined with income Al earned from his other clients, to help keep the Mungers comfortable during the Depression. Charlie also helped the family by working to earn his own spending money and thus learned firsthand the value of financial independence.

幸运的是，阿尔·芒格的律师事务所在大萧条中生意兴隆；当美国最高法院（Supreme Court）同意复审一桩涉及他代理的小型肥皂制造公司的税务案时，更是锦上添花。碰巧，巨头高露洁-棕榄公司（Colgate-Palmolive Company17Colgate-Palmolive Company高露洁-棕榄公司）也受该判决影响。高露洁担心这位中西部律师缺乏在最高法院成功辩护的必备经验，便慷慨付钱给阿尔，让他让贤，由一位著名的纽约律师取而代之。那位大城市的律师输掉了官司，而阿尔则把一笔可观的律师费装进了口袋。后来，阿尔开玩笑说，他本来也可以少收很多费用、照样输掉这场官司。这笔费用的具体数额从未公开，但它与阿尔从其他客户那里赚得的收入合在一起，足以让芒格一家在大萧条中维持宽裕。查理也通过打工挣自己的零花钱来帮补家用，由此切身体会到了财务独立的价值。

In 1941, as the war raged across the Atlantic, Charlie graduated from Central High School and left Omaha for the University of Michigan. There he chose mathematics as his major, drawn by the appeal of numerical logic and reason. He also discovered physics after enrolling in a basic course to fulfill an academic requirement for science. Charlie was fascinated by the power of physics and its boundless reach. In particular, he was impressed by the process followed by physicists such as Albert Einstein to address the unknown. Physics-like problem-solving was to become a passion for Charlie and is a skill he considers helpful in framing the problems of life. He has often stated that anyone who wants to be successful should study physics because its concepts and formulas so beautifully demonstrate the powers of sound theory.

1941年，大西洋彼岸战火纷飞，查理从中央高中毕业，离开奥马哈，前往密歇根大学19The University of Michigan密歇根大学（University of Michigan）。在那里，他被数字逻辑与推理的魅力吸引，选择数学为专业。修读一门满足理科必修要求的基础课程后，他又迷上了物理学。查理为物理学的威力及其无垠的疆域所着迷。尤其令他印象深刻的，是阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦（Albert Einstein）等物理学家探究未知的过程。像物理学那样解决问题，日后成了查理的挚爱，也被他视为一种有助于框定人生难题的技能。他常说，任何想成功的人都应该学习物理学，因为其概念与公式如此优美地展现了可靠理论的力量。

“Charlie has often stated that anyone who wants to be successful should study physics because its concepts and formulas so beautifully demonstrate the powers of sound theory.”查理常说，任何想成功的人都该学物理，因为物理的概念与公式如此优美地展示了扎实理论的力量。

College-aged men were then in high demand for military service. Days after turning 19 and completing his second year at Michigan, Charlie enlisted in the Army Air Corps19Army Air Corps陆军航空队 in a program that would eventually make him a second lieutenant. He was sent to the Albuquerque campus of the University of New Mexico for studies in general science and engineering. Next, he was shuffled to the prestigious California Institute of Technology in Pasadena. He was schooled in thermodynamics and the science of meteorology—then essential to flyers—and trained to become a meteorologist. After completing his studies at Caltech, Charlie was dispatched to a permanent duty station in Nome, Alaska.

那时，适龄大学男生被军方大量征召。刚满19岁、在密歇根读完大二的查理，便参加了陆军航空队19Army Air Corps陆军航空队（Army Air Corps）的一个培养计划，最终将成为一名少尉。他被派往新墨西哥大学（University of New Mexico）的阿尔伯克基（Albuquerque）校区，学习普通科学与工程。接着，他又被调往帕萨迪纳（Pasadena）声名卓著的加州理工学院（California Institute of Technology，简称 Caltech）。他学习了热力学和气象科学——当时对飞行员至关重要——并被训练成一名气象学家。在加州理工完成学业后，查理被派往阿拉斯加州（Alaska）诺姆（Nome）的永久驻地。

While still in the service, he married Nancy Huggins, a young woman from Pasadena who was a good friend of his sister Mary at Scripps College. They were stationed in Albuquerque and then San Antonio until Charlie was discharged from the Army Air Corps in 1946. Soon Charlie and Nancy had their first child, a boy whom they named Teddy.21Harvard哈佛大学

还在服役期间，他与南希·哈金斯（Nancy Huggins）结婚；这位来自帕萨迪纳的姑娘，是妹妹玛丽在斯克里普斯学院（Scripps College）的好友。他们先后驻扎在阿尔伯克基和圣安东尼奥（San Antonio），直到1946年查理从陆军航空队退役。不久，查理和南希有了第一个孩子，是个男孩，取名泰迪（Teddy）。

Although he had attended several universities, Charlie still did not have a bachelor’s degree. Nevertheless, using the GI Bill, he applied to Harvard Law School, where his father had preceded him. His lack of an undergraduate degree threatened to derail him, but a family friend, former Harvard Law School dean Roscoe Pound, interceded on Charlie’s behalf. Charlie was admitted, despite the determination of the admissions office to first send him back to college.

尽管上过好几所大学，查理仍没有学士学位。不过，他凭借《退伍军人权利法案》（GI Bill）申请了哈佛法学院（Harvard Law School）——他父亲也曾就读于此。缺少本科学位险些让他折戟，但一位世交、哈佛法学院前院长罗斯科·庞德（Roscoe Pound）为他出面说项。查理被录取了，尽管招生办原本铁了心要先把他退回大学。

As it turned out, Charlie had little trouble succeeding at Harvard, though he annoyed a few people along the way. Because of his intellect (the Army measured his IQ at the top of the curve), Charlie had a tendency to be abrupt, which was often interpreted as rudeness. Actually, Charlie was just in a hurry, and the customary pleasantries of the classroom were of little concern to him. Even so, he was liked by most of his peers and fully enjoyed the social aspects of student life in Cambridge.

结果，查理在哈佛毫不费力地取得了成功，尽管途中得罪了几个人。由于才智过人（军队测得其智商处于曲线顶端），查理往往说话唐突，常被误解为无礼。其实查理只是性子急，对课堂上那些客套寒暄并不在意。即便如此，他仍受大多数同辈喜爱，并充分享受了在坎布里奇（Cambridge）的学生生活的社交一面。

“Charlie had little trouble succeeding at Harvard, though he annoyed a few people along the way.”查理在哈佛顺风顺水，尽管途中惹恼了少许人。

Charlie graduated from Harvard Law School in 1948 and was one of 12 in his class of 335 to graduate magna cum laude. He considered joining his father’s law practice, but after a discussion with his father, both of them concluded that Charlie should try a larger city. He headed off to Southern California, a place he had liked while a student at Caltech. After passing the California bar exam, he joined the firm of Wright & Garrett, later renamed Musick, Peeler & Garrett. Charlie built a house, designed by his architect uncle, Frederick Stott, in South Pasadena, where he and Nancy and their three children, Teddy, Molly, and Wendy, lived.

查理1948年从哈佛法学院毕业，在335人的同届中，以优异成绩（magna cum laude）成为12名优秀毕业生之一。他考虑过加入父亲的律师事务所，但与父亲商议后，两人一致认为查理应该去更大的城市发展。他动身前往南加州——那是他在加州理工求学时就喜欢的地方。通过加州律师资格考试后，他加入了赖特与加雷特（Wright & Garrett）律师事务所，该所后来更名为穆西克、皮勒与加雷特（Musick, Peeler & Garrett）。查理在南帕萨迪纳（South Pasadena）建了一座房子，由他的建筑师舅舅弗雷德里克·斯托特（Frederick Stott）设计；他和南希以及三个孩子——泰迪、莫莉（Molly）和温迪（Wendy）——住在那里。

Despite outward appearances, all was not sunny in Charlie’s world. His marriage was in trouble, and he and his wife finally divorced in 1953. Not long thereafter, Charlie learned that his adored son, Teddy, was terminally ill with leukemia. It was a significant burden for 29-year-old Charlie. In that era, before bone marrow transplants, there was no hope. A friend remembers that Charlie would visit his dying son in the hospital and then walk the streets of Pasadena crying.

尽管外表光鲜，查理的世界并非一片晴空。他的婚姻出了问题，最终在1953年与妻子离婚。此后不久，查理得知他深爱的儿子泰迪罹患白血病，已是晚期。对29岁的查理来说，这是沉重的负担。在那个时代，骨髓移植尚未出现，毫无希望可言。一位朋友记得，查理会去医院探望濒死的儿子，然后走在帕萨迪纳的街道上哭泣。

During this sad time, his friend and law partner, Roy Tolles,24Roy Tolles罗伊·托尔斯 arranged through a friend for Charlie to meet Nancy Barry Borthwick, who lived in Los Angeles. She was a Stanford graduate and had two small boys, close to the ages of his girls. Charlie and Nancy had much in common and had fun together, and after a few months of dating became engaged. They were married in a small family wedding in January 1956, and all four children—his girls and her boys, aged 4 to 7—attended the wedding.

在这段悲伤的日子里，他的朋友兼律所合伙人罗伊·托尔斯24Roy Tolles罗伊·托尔斯（Roy Tolles）通过一位朋友安排查理与住在洛杉矶的南希·巴里·博斯威克（Nancy Barry Borthwick）见面。她是斯坦福（Stanford）毕业生，有两个年幼的男孩，年纪与他家的女孩相仿。查理和南希志趣相投，相处甚欢，约会数月后便订了婚。他们在1956年1月举办了一场小型家庭婚礼，四个孩子——他的女儿们和她的儿子们，年龄从四岁到七岁——都出席了婚礼。

Charlie and Nancy lived in her house in the hills of West Los Angeles for several years. Then, partly to shorten Charlie’s daily commute, they moved to Hancock Park, where they still reside. The house they built there was large enough for their ever-expanding family: three more boys and a girl, for a total of eight. Fortunately, both liked children! They also liked golf, the beach, and social clubs. Charlie and Nancy were soon members of the University Club, the California Club, the Los Angeles Country Club, and the Beach Club.

查理和南希在她位于洛杉矶西部丘陵地带的房子里住了几年。后来，部分为了缩短查理每天的通勤，他们搬到了汉考克公园（Hancock Park），至今仍住在那里。他们在那里建的房子足够容纳不断壮大的家庭：又添了三个男孩和一个女孩，总共八个孩子。幸运的是，两人都喜欢孩子！他们也喜欢高尔夫、海滩和社交俱乐部。查理和南希很快成了大学俱乐部（University Club）、加州俱乐部（California Club）、洛杉矶乡村俱乐部（Los Angeles Country Club）和海滩俱乐部（Beach Club）的成员。

fig 21
—
Charlie, Nancy, and their family查理、南希和他们的家人

With many new responsibilities, Charlie worked hard at his law practice.22Charlie in law practice查理执业律师时期 Even so, his earnings were unsatisfactory to him as they were based on a combination of billable hours and seniority. He wanted more than what a senior law partner would be able to earn. He sought to be like his firm’s leading capitalist clients, in particular the universally admired Harvey Mudd, later the founder of the college bearing his name. With Nancy’s support, he turned to outside ventures and alternative ways to generate income. However, he never forgot the sound principles taught by his grandfather: to concentrate on the task immediately in front of him and to control spending.

肩负诸多新责任，查理在律师业务上十分卖力。即便如此，收入仍不能令他满意，因为收入取决于计费工时和资历。他想要的，不止于资深合伙人的所得。他渴望像事务所里那些顶尖的资本家客户一样，尤其是那位人人敬仰的哈维·马德（Harvey Mudd）——后来创办了以他名字命名的学院。在南希的支持下，他转向外部投资和别的创收门道。不过，他从未忘记祖父传授的稳健原则：专注眼前的事务，控制开支。

“Charlie never forgot the sound principles taught by his grandfather: to concentrate on the task immediately in front of him and to controlxa0spending.”查理从未忘记祖父教导的稳健原则：专注于眼前的事，并控制开销。

Following this conservative approach, Charlie seized opportunities to build wealth. He began investing in stocks and acquired equity in one of his clients’ electronics businesses, a practice common among lawyers in the mid-1950s and 1960s. This investment was mutually beneficial: Charlie gained invaluable knowledge about business, while his client enjoyed the proactive attention of a lawyer who knew more than just the law.

秉持这种保守的方法，查理抓住机会积累财富。他开始投资股票，并取得了某位客户一家电子企业的股权——这种做法在20世纪50年代中期到60年代的律师中很普遍。这项投资互利互惠：查理获得了宝贵的经商知识，而客户则享受到了一位不只懂法律的律师主动而周到的关照。

In 1961, Charlie tackled property development for the first time, in partnership with Otis Booth,23Otis Booth奥蒂斯·布思 a client and friend. The venture, building condominiums on land near Caltech, was a smashing success, and the partners earned a handsome profit of $300,000 on a $100,000 investment. Charlie and Otis then undertook other successful construction and development projects in Pasadena. Later, Charlie participated in similar projects in Alhambra, California. He sharpened his business acumen by handling the negotiations and contracts. In all cases, he left all of his profits in real estate ventures so that bigger and bigger projects became possible. When he stopped in 1964, he had a nest egg of $1.4 million from real estate projects alone.

1961年，查理首次涉足房地产开发，合伙对象是客户兼朋友奥蒂斯·布思23Otis Booth奥蒂斯·布思（Otis Booth）。他们在加州理工附近的地块上建造公寓，大获成功，合伙人以10万美元的投资赚得30万美元的丰厚利润。查理和奥蒂斯随后在帕萨迪纳又承接了其他成功的建筑与开发项目。后来，查理还在加州阿罕布拉（Alhambra）参与了类似项目。通过经手谈判与合同，他的商业敏锐度愈发精进。在所有这些项目中，他都把利润全部再投入房地产，于是项目越做越大成为可能。1964年收手时，单是房地产项目就为他攒下了140万美元的储备金。

In February 1962, he joined four colleagues from Musick, Peeler & Garrett in establishing a new law firm. The original partners were Roy Tolles,24Roy Tolles罗伊·托尔斯 Rod Hills, Dick Esbenshade, Fred Warder, and Charlie. They were joined by Rod’s wife, Carla, and James T. Wood, a sole practitioner and friend of the Hills. They named the firm Munger, Tolles & Hills. Over the years, the firm had several names, always beginning with Munger, Tolles. With the addition of Ron Olson, it finally became Munger, Tolles & Olson, shortened as Munger, Tolles or MTO.

1962年2月，他与来自穆西克、皮勒与加雷特的四位同事共同创办了一家新律所。最初的合伙人有罗伊·托尔斯、罗德·希尔斯（Rod Hills）、迪克·埃斯本沙德（Dick Esbenshade）、弗雷德·沃德（Fred Warder）和查理。罗德之妻卡拉（Carla）以及詹姆斯·T·伍德（James T. Wood）——一位独立执业律师、希尔斯家的朋友——也加入了他们。他们将律所命名为芒格、托尔斯与希尔斯（Munger, Tolles & Hills）。多年间，这家律所几易其名，但始终以“芒格、托尔斯”开头。随着罗恩·奥尔森（Ron Olson）的加入，它最终成为芒格、托尔斯与奥尔森（Munger, Tolles & Olson），简称芒格托尔斯（Munger Tolles）或 MTO。

The successful practice of law was by then a backstop rather than an ending objective for Charlie. At about the time that he was launching his new law firm, he was carefully crafting his exit plan. Charlie set up an investment partnership with Jack Wheeler, and they were later joined by Al Marshall. The idea for this partnership arose a few years earlier when the death of Charlie’s father required him to return to Omaha to administer the estate. To welcome him home, the children of Charlie’s friend and medical mentor, Dr. Ed Davis, arranged for a dinner party. Both of the Davis boys, Eddie Jr. and Neil, were former childhood chums of Charlie and were now physicians, while their sister Willa had married an Omaha businessman, Lee Seemann. The dinner party included Willa and Lee, Neil and his wife Joan, and a fellow named Warren Buffett.25Warren Buffett沃伦·巴菲特

那时，成功的律师业务对查理而言已是一个退路，而非终极目标。大约在创办新律所的同时，他就在精心谋划退出方案。查理与杰克·惠勒（Jack Wheeler）设立了一个投资合伙，后来艾尔·马歇尔（Al Marshall）也加入了。这个合伙的念头源于几年前：查理父亲去世，他必须返回奥马哈料理遗产。为了欢迎他回家，查理的朋友兼医学导师埃德·戴维斯医生的子女安排了一场晚宴。戴维斯的两个儿子小埃迪（Eddie Jr.）和尼尔（Neil）都是查理儿时的玩伴，如今都成了医生；他们的妹妹薇拉（Willa）则嫁给了奥马哈商人李·西曼（Lee Seemann）。晚宴的宾客有薇拉和李、尼尔及其妻子琼（Joan），还有一位叫沃伦·巴菲特的小伙子。

Charlie recognized Warren’s family name from his days at Buffett & Son, and Warren had heard of Charlie a few years earlier when he was raising investment capital in Omaha. At one point, Warren had met with Dr. Davis and his wife, Dorothy, to explain his investment philosophy, and they agreed to place a large part of their life savings—$100,000—with him. Why? The doctor explained that Warren reminded him of Charlie Munger. Warren didn’t know Charlie but already had at least one good reason to like him.

查理从自己在巴菲特父子店的岁月认出了沃伦的姓氏；而沃伦几年前在奥马哈筹措投资资本时，也听说过查理。有一次，沃伦见了戴维斯医生及其妻子多萝西（Dorothy），阐释自己的投资哲学，他们同意将毕生积蓄的一大部分——10万美元——交给他打理。为什么？医生解释说，沃伦让他想起了查理·芒格。沃伦并不认识查理，但已经至少有一个喜欢他的好理由了。

“Warren didn’t know Charlie but already had at least one good reason to likexa0him.”沃伦还不认识查理，却已至少有个充分的理由喜欢他。

During the homecoming dinner, Charlie and Warren realized they shared many ideas. It also became evident to the others at the table that this was going to be a two-way conversation. As the evening progressed, the two young men—Warren was 29 and Charlie 35—became engrossed in a wide-ranging dialogue26Warren and Charlie沃伦与查理 covering many aspects of business, finance, and history. Where one was knowledgeable, the other was just as excited to learn.

在那场回乡晚宴上，查理和沃伦意识到他们有许多共同的想法。桌上其他人也明显看出，这将是一场双向的对话。随着夜色渐深，这两位年轻人——沃伦29岁，查理35岁——沉浸在一场包罗商业、金融与历史诸多方面的广泛对话中。一方所知，另一方同样兴味盎然地求教。

Warren was unenthusiastic about Charlie’s continued practice of law. He said that while law might be a good hobby for Charlie, it was a far less promising business than what Warren was doing. Warren’s logic helped Charlie to decide to quit law practice at the earliest point he could afford to do so.

沃伦对查理继续从事律师业并不热心。他说，当律师对查理或许是个不错的爱好，但比起沃伦所做的事，这门生意的前景差得太远。沃伦的逻辑促使查理下定决心，在力所能及的最早时机退出律师行当。

When Charlie returned to Los Angeles, the conversations continued via telephone and lengthy letters, sometimes as long as nine pages. It was evident to both that they were meant to be in business together. There was no formal partnership or contractual relationship—the bond was created by a handshake and backed by two Midwesterners who understood and respected the value of one’s word.

查理回到洛杉矶后，对话通过电话和长信继续，有时信长达九页。两人都清楚，他们注定要一起经商。没有什么正式的合伙或契约关系——这份纽带由一次握手缔结，由两位懂得并尊重一诺千金的中西部人作保。

“There was no formal partnership or contractual relationship—the bond was created by a handshake and backed by two Midwesterners who understood and respected the value of one’sxa0word.”并无正式的合伙或合同关系——这份纽带由一次握手铸就，并由两位懂得并尊重『一诺千金』价值的中西部人作保。

There were many benefits to their partnership: friendship, investment opportunities, and the unique ability to grasp each other’s ideas and observations. Later, the two organizations they headed were also beneficiaries. As Warren was investing in and acquiring companies, he sent business to Munger, Tolles, a practice that allowed him over time to benefit from having one of the nation’s top law firms at his disposal. Munger, Tolles, meanwhile, not only got Buffett’s legal fees but also gained because his reputation attracted other blue-chip clients to the firm.

他们的合伙带来诸多益处：友谊、投资机会，以及理解彼此想法与见解的独特能力。后来，他们各自执掌的两家机构也成了受益者。沃伦在投资和收购公司时，把业务交给芒格托尔斯，这种做法让他长期受益于随时可用的一家全国顶尖律所。与此同时，芒格托尔斯不仅拿到了巴菲特的法律费，还因为他的声望为律所招来了其他蓝筹客户。

Munger, Tolles is not just about money, though. Mirroring the way Charlie conducts his personal life, the firm has an enviable record of quietly providing pro bono assistance to support groups for impoverished and disadvantaged people in the Los Angeles community. ‘To this day, Charlie continues to influence the firm’s attorneys, reminding them, “You don’t need to take the last dollar” and “Choose clients as you would friends.” Though Charlie left the firm as an active partner in 1965 after only three years, his indelible influence remains, as indicated by the fact that his name still heads the listing of 175 attorneys. When he left, he didn’t take his share of the firm’s capital. Instead, he directed that his share go to the estate of his young partner, Fred Warder, who left behind a wife and children when he died of cancer.

不过，芒格托尔斯并非只为钱。呼应查理的个人行事方式，该所在洛杉矶社区默默为贫困和弱势群体的支援组织提供公益法律援助，成绩令人称羡。时至今日，查理仍影响着律所的律师们，提醒他们“不必非要赚到最后一美元”以及“像选朋友那样选客户”。尽管查理在1965年——仅仅三年后——便以活跃合伙人身份离开了律所，他不可磨灭的影响仍在，这体现在他的名字至今仍列于175名律师的榜首。离开时，他没有拿走自己在律所的资本份额，而是将其指定划归年轻合伙人弗雷德·沃德的遗产——沃德死于癌症，留下妻儿。

“To this day, Charlie continues to influence the firm’s attorneys, reminding them, ‘You don’t need to take the last dollar’ and ‘Choose clients as you wouldxa0friends.’”时至今日，查理仍在影响着公司的律师们，提醒他们：『不必赚走最后一个子儿』，以及『选客户要像选朋友一样。』

Charlie’s plan for financial independence was soon working with great success. He spent much time building the asset base of Wheeler, Munger & Co., his investment partnership with Jack Wheeler. He also spent time working on various real estate developments. All was going as planned, with no significant reverses. At Wheeler, Munger & Co., Charlie was investing in stocks partly with his own money and partly with other people’s money. Charlie concentrated more on putting his capital to work than attracting new clients. Because Jack Wheeler held two seats on the Pacific Coast Stock Exchange, the partnership paid low trading commissions while Wheeler, Munger kept the overhead cost at close to zero.

查理的财务独立计划很快大获成功。他花大量时间打造惠勒、芒格与公司（Wheeler, Munger & Co.）的资产基础——这是他与杰克·惠勒的投资合伙。他还花时间参与各类房地产开发。一切按部就班，没有重大挫折。在惠勒、芒格公司，查理投资股票，部分用自有资金，部分用他人的资金。查理更专注于让资本运转起来，而非招揽新客户。由于杰克·惠勒在太平洋海岸证券交易所（Pacific Coast Stock Exchange）拥有两个席位，这家合伙只需支付很低的交易佣金，而惠勒、芒格将运营开支保持在近乎为零。

As time passed, Charlie and Warren kept up their frequent telephone conversations and letters, sharing ideas and investment concepts. Sometimes they would agree to invest in the same company. Other times they went in different directions. In time, their independent portfolios had overlapping investments. Warren invested in the Blue Chip Stamp Co.27Blue Chip Stamp Company蓝筹印花公司 and became the largest single shareholder. Charlie became the second-largest shareholder, and, eventually, Berkshire Hathaway ended up acquiring the company.

随着时间推移，查理和沃伦保持着频繁的电话与书信往来，分享想法与投资理念。有时他们会约定投资同一家公司；有时则分道扬镳。久而久之，他们各自独立的投资组合出现了重叠。沃伦投资了蓝筹印花公司（Blue Chip Stamp Co.27Blue Chip Stamp Company蓝筹印花公司），成为最大的单一股东。查理成为第二大股东，最终，伯克希尔·哈撒韦将这家公司收购。

Charlie built the Wheeler, Munger partnership from 1962 through 1975. It did exceptionally well for the first 11 years, compounding at 28.3 percent gross (20 percent net) versus 6.7 percent for the Dow, without a single down year. But the partnership was hit hard in the vicious bear market of 1973 and 1974 when it fell 31.9 percent and 31.5 percent in back-to-back years, as the partnership’s largest holdings, Blue Chip Stamps and New America Fund, fell sharply. This decline was despite, as Charlie puts it, “having its major investments virtually sure of eventually being saleable at prices higher than the quoted market prices.” But the partnership rebounded strongly in 1975, rising 73.2 percent, bringing the overall record over 14 years to 19.8 percent (13.7 percent net) compounded annual returns versus 5 percent for the Dow.

查理在1962至1975年间打造了这个惠勒、芒格合伙。头11年表现极为出色，毛复合收益率28.3%（净收益率20%），而道指（Dow）仅6.7%，且无一亏损之年。但合伙在1973和1974年的凶猛熊市中遭受重创，连续两年分别下跌31.9%和31.5%，因为合伙的重仓股蓝筹印花和新美国基金（New America Fund）大幅下挫。尽管如查理所言，“其主要投资几乎笃定最终能以高于市场报价的价格售出”，跌势依旧。不过，合伙在1975年强劲反弹，上涨73.2%，使14年的整体纪录达到19.8%的年均复合回报（净13.7%），而道指仅5%。

After this difficult experience, Charlie followed Warren in concluding that he no longer wanted to manage funds directly for investors. (Warren had closed his own partnerships in 1969.) Instead, they resolved to build equity through stock ownership in a holding company. When Wheeler, Munger was liquidated, its stakeholders received shares in Blue Chip Stamps and Diversified Retailing. Later, these shares were converted into Berkshire Hathaway stock,28Berkshire Hathaway Stock伯克希尔·哈撒韦股票 which ended 1975 at $38. Today, each share is worth more than $85,000, making Charlie a member of the Forbes list30Charlie in Forbes查理登上《福布斯》 of the 400 wealthiest individuals. While he doesn’t mind the wealth, he regrets having his name on any such list. Despite his healthy self-image, Charlie would prefer to be anonymous.

历经这段艰难，查理追随沃伦，断定自己再也不想直接为投资者管理基金了。（沃伦已于1969年关闭了自己的合伙。）取而代之，他们决意通过在一家控股公司持股来积累权益。惠勒、芒格清算时，其权益持有人得到了蓝筹印花和多元零售（Diversified Retailing）的股份。后来，这些股份被转换为伯克希尔·哈撒韦的股票，1975年底收于38美元。如今，每股价值超过8.5万美元，使查理跻身《福布斯30Charlie in Forbes查理登上《福布斯》》（Forbes）400富豪榜。虽然他不介意财富，却为自己出现在任何此类榜单上感到遗憾。尽管自我形象健康，查理还是宁愿默默无闻。

The story of Berkshire Hathaway’s extraordinary success under Warren and Charlie’s leadership has been told many times elsewhere, so the details won’t be repeated here. To summarize, however, they have a spectacular track record of identifying undervalued companies and then either buying large stakes in the public markets or acquiring them outright. Regarding the latter, they have acquired a diverse assortment of businesses such as Johns Manville, The Buffalo Evening News, FlightSafety International, NetJets, Shaw Carpet, Benjamin Moore, GEICO, and Dairy Queen. In addition, they have purchased meaningful stakes in public companies such as The Washington Post, Coca-Cola, Gillette, and American Express. For the most part, they have held their major investments for the long term—in fact, they still own almost every business they’ve ever acquired outright.

伯克希尔·哈撒韦在沃伦和查理领导下取得非凡成功的故事，已在别处被讲述过许多次，故细节此处不再赘述。不过概括而言，他们在识别被低估的公司、继而在公开市场上买入大量股份或直接整体收购方面，有着辉煌的业绩纪录。就后者而言，他们收购了形形色色的企业，如约翰斯·曼维尔（Johns Manville）、布法罗晚报（The Buffalo Evening News）、飞安国际（FlightSafety International）、NetJets、肖氏地毯（Shaw Carpet）、本杰明·摩尔涂料（Benjamin Moore Paint）、GEICO 和冰雪皇后（Dairy Queen）。此外，他们还在华盛顿邮报（The Washington Post）、可口可乐（Coca-Cola）、吉列（Gillette）和美国运通（American Express）等上市公司中购入了可观的股份。在大多数情况下，他们长期持有主要投资——事实上，他们几乎仍拥有每一家曾经整体收购的企业。

Charlie’s affinity for Benjamin Franklin’s expansive career in government, business, finance, and industry can be found in his many speeches and whenever he holds an audience, large or small. At the 75th anniversary of See’s Candies, Charlie said:

查理对本杰明·富兰克林横跨政府、商业、金融与工业的广阔生涯的认同，见于他的诸多演讲，也见于他每次面对听众——无论大小——之时。在喜诗糖果（See's Candies）75周年庆典上，查理说道

I am a biography nut myself. And I think when you’re trying to teach the great concepts that work, it helps to tie them into the lives and personalities of the people who developed them. I think you learn economics better if you make Adam Smith your friend. That sounds funny, making friends among the “eminent dead,” but if you go through life making friends with the eminent dead who had the right ideas, I think it will work better for you in life and work better in education. It’s way better than just giving the basic concepts.

我自己就是个传记迷。而且我认为，当你试图传授那些行之有效的伟大概念时，把它们和发展这些概念的人的生活与个性联系起来，会很有帮助。我认为，如果你让亚当·斯密（Adam Smith）成为你的朋友，你会把经济学学得更好。这听起来很滑稽——在“逝去的伟人”中间交朋友——但如果你在生活中不断和那些拥有正确思想的逝去伟人交朋友，我认为它会让你的生活更顺遂，也让教育更有效。这远比只给你讲基本概念要好得多。

“If you go through life making friends with the eminent dead who had the right ideas, I think it will work better for you in life and work better in education.”如果你一生都与那些思想正确的已故贤人为友，我想这于人生更有助益，于求学也更见效。

Franklin used his self-made wealth to achieve financial independence so he could concentrate on societal improvement. Charlie admires that trait in his mentor and strives to emulate Franklin. He has had a long involvement with Good Samaritan Hospital and Harvard-Westlake School, both in Los Angeles, and has chaired the boards of each. He and Nancy have also long supported Stanford University and the Huntington Library, Art Collections, and Botanical Gardens in San Marino, California. They provided funding for a major expansion to the Huntington called the Munger Research Center. Although Charlie is a self-described conservative Republican, chief among his causes is Planned Parenthood. He believes that every child deserves to be born to a welcoming mother. He also supports efforts to improve the environment and the quality of education. As the father of 8 and grandfather of 16, Charlie regards his legacy as helping future generations inherit a better world.

富兰克林用他白手起家的财富实现了财务独立，从而能够专注于社会改良。查理景仰导师身上的这一特质，并努力效仿富兰克林。他长期参与洛杉矶的好撒玛利亚医院（Good Samaritan Hospital）和哈佛-西湖学校（Harvard-Westlake School），并曾担任两者的董事会主席。他和南希也长期支持斯坦福大学，以及加州圣马里诺（San Marino）的亨廷顿图书馆艺术收藏与植物园（Huntington Library Art Collections and Botanical Gardens）。他们最近为亨廷顿一项名为芒格研究中心（Munger Research Center）的重大扩建提供了资金。尽管查理自称为保守派共和党人，但他最为看重的事业却是计划生育协会（Planned Parenthood）。他相信，每个孩子都理应降生在一个欢迎他的母亲怀里。他也支持改善环境与教育质量的努力。作为8个孩子的父亲和16个孙辈的祖父，查理将自己的遗产视为：帮助后代继承一个更美好的世界。
